questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook tasty meals using insects
Why we dislike some foods and if we can change
The healthiest foods for growing children
Why Japanese food is becoming popular abroad
questions.why: They hear from food experts about why we hate some foods and whether we can learn to love them.

questions.q: What does Neil say about umeboshi?
options: He has never tried it, but he wants to
He has always loved it, since he was a child
He still can't eat it, even after many tries
He didn't like it at first, but now loves it
questions.why: He really didn't like it at first, but got used to it and now really loves it.

questions.q: What food did Becca learn to love as she got older?
options: Prawns
Coriander
Olives
Chocolate
questions.why: Becca says she used to hate olives but has grown to love them.

questions.q: According to Dr Dana Small, where do food dislikes come from?
options: Both our genes and what we learn
Only our genes
Only what our parents taught us
Mostly from the country we live in
questions.why: Asked if dislikes are learned or genetic, she says 'Ah, both!'

questions.q: What example of a genetic difference does Dana give?
options: Some people can't eat nuts without getting ill
Some people are born loving sweets and sugar
Some people can't taste salt in their food
Some people smell or taste coriander differently
questions.why: She says you could, via genetics, smell or taste coriander differently.

questions.q: What is the 'masking' technique that Claire Thornton Wood uses?
options: Hiding food so children can't see it
Dipping a food you dislike into one you like
Eating with your eyes closed
Cooking food until it has no taste
questions.why: She says masking is where you dip a food you don't like into something you do like.

questions.q: Why does Claire offer chocolate-covered insects to parents?
options: To show the idea of a food can put us off
To prove that insects are healthier than meat
To make them feel sick as part of a test
To sell more of her own chocolate products
questions.why: People find there's nothing 'inherently unpleasant' about them; it's the concept of an insect.

questions.q: According to Claire, what can cause a fear of a certain food?
options: Seeing it on television cooking shows
Never having tried it as a child
Having been ill after eating it before
Eating it far too often for many years
questions.why: She says if a dodgy prawn made you unwell, you might avoid prawns: fear-based avoidance.
